rationale: Both keep the children's allergies, medicines and emergency contacts on a page in the shared family folder (F043) and turn them, by a prompt rule on the parent's own agent, into a page the parent prints, forwards or pastes (the emergency plan, the sitter sheet, the answers for a school, camp or sports form), which is the reason round 1 gave for putting the sitter sheet on this card; kept apart, the same facts are typed in twice, once into CRT-13's plan page and once into CRT-12's per-child form-facts section. No earlier round proposed or ruled on this pair, both are medium risk on the parent's own agent with nothing sent, filled in or submitted by Happy, and CRT-12's wave C rests on no later dependency (the family folder, the household store, photo and PDF reading and reminders are all wave A), so the whole can ship in wave B on a card that states its parts separately: the emergency plan and sitter sheet, the fixed reply to emergency phrases, and the document index with form due dates and paste-ready answers, whose drafting sends the children's health facts to the cloud model.
name: Family paperwork from one set of facts: the emergency card, the sitter sheet, and a school, camp and health-form kit (document index, due dates, paste-ready answers), plus a fixed reply to emergency texts

rationale: Search by meaning is not a feature of its own but one setting (the memory search provider switched to an embedding model on the Mac mini) on the same memory search that F041 grants to each parent's agent and that also indexes the shared handbook folder (F043), and F041's own caveat already says its search is by keyword only until F046 is added. F046's 'later' wave was inherited from the skipped local-model milestone, which its own correction says the embedding-only setup does not need, and it adds no tool, no agent and no way to send anything out (low risk, value 2), so no dependency or new kind of risk separates the two: it becomes a named later, optional step on the wave A card, in the way the natural voice is a later step on F003, with the provider plugin install and the model download stated as that step's own prerequisite and decision.
name: Durable per-person memory: 'remember this' is saved to that parent's own notes and found again, by keyword first and by meaning as a later step (local embeddings, text only)

rationale: Both are what a parent types into the thread to control Happy itself, and each record describes the other as the second level of one stop control (/stop ends one answer in one chat, the phrase stops everything), while OCL-06 builds nothing except a one-screen cheat sheet for the parents and one config choice; round 3's purpose pass proposed this pair and it was not taken up, with no verdict in either history, and what that pass did not say is that G005's own caveat keeps both phrases out of Happy's help text and replies, so a parent learns them only from paper (that cheat sheet and, for the second adult, the recovery card CRT-05), yet the sheet is specified with the five commands alone and would have to be written twice. Both are wave A and low risk and neither adds a tool, a recipient or a data source, so no rule above is crossed: the card says which part works today (the built-in commands) and which needs the in-house plugin (the stop and lock-out phrases), keeps Tony's choice about leaving /restart and /update reachable from chat, and leaves mute and vacation mode with the notification policy (G001).
name: Controlling Happy by text: the built-in commands (/stop, /new, /status, /usage, /tools) and the stop-everything and lock-out phrases
